Q: Double Summation in Python A:

# Function returning a pair of values

def get_key_value_pair(2):

return "key", "value"

# Ignoring the first element of the returned pair using a single underscore

_, value = get_key_value_pair()

# The first element is ignored, and only the second element is used

print("Value:", value)

Q: How to stream OpenAI API response chunks from FastAPI to a Next.js 14 App Router frontend using Server-Sent Events (SSE)? A:

Your FastAPI backend code looks correct — StreamingResponse with a proper async generator and the right headers should stream token-by-token. A few things to check, in order of likelihood: 1. Isolate the backend first. Test the FastAPI endpoint directly with curl -N (the -N disables curl's own buffering): curl -N -X POST https://your-railway-url/chat -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'. If tokens arrive progressively here, the backend is fine and the bug is downstream (Next.js). If they arrive all at once even here, it's likely GZipMiddleware or another response-compressing middleware buffering the full stream before compressing — check app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware...) and remove/exclude it for this route. 2. Check your Next.js API route (the code you haven't shown). Your frontend fetches /api/chat, which is a Next.js route handler proxying to FastAPI — not FastAPI directly. If that handler does something like const res = await fetch(fastapiUrl, ...); return NextResponse.json(await res.json()), it fully buffers the response before returning anything. You need the route handler to forward the ReadableStream directly: add export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' at the top of the file, then in your POST handler do const res = await fetch(fastapiUrl, { method: 'POST', body: await req.text() }); return new Response(res.body, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } }). The force-dynamic export matters — without it, Next.js may try to statically optimize or cache the route, which breaks streaming. 3. Vercel-specific gotcha: if this route runs on Vercel's Node.js serverless runtime (not Edge), some Vercel setups buffer function output. If step 2's fix doesn't work, try adding export const runtime = 'edge' to the route. Start with step 1 — it tells you immediately whether the bug is in FastAPI or in the Next.js proxy layer.

Q: The requested url was rejected A:

You are block by a firewall ASM. The data you are trying to pass are detected as threats and your request is denied. You need to resolve this with you Network engineer by providing him the ID.

NOTE: Cookies cleanup might also work sometimes!

Q: Continue a project from a different machine A:

The upper right of your repo directory there's a green button (<> Code) that has 3 different ways to clone the repo to the new machine. Generally, the easiest way is with GitHub CLI using this command:

gh repo clone user/repo

It creates a new folder with your repo's name where you run it, you'll need to authenticate. Make sure to pull code regularly before you push to avoid merge conflicts. Also look into branching and merging to make sure your code stays clean!
